3755.title: Morocco Cycling Tour: Atlas Mountains & Sahara Desert

tab_content.1_wpeditor:
Eight days, six of them on the bike, from Marrakech over the High Atlas to the edge of the Sahara. You ride past Ait Ben Haddou, down through the palm groves of the Draa Valley, across dry lakes and out to the Chegaga dunes, where you spend a night under a sky full of stars.

The riding is mostly on quiet back roads and desert tracks, so it suits a mountain bike, a gravel bike or an e-bike. A 4x4 support vehicle stays with the group every day, so you can take a break in the car whenever you need one.

Trip details

  • Tour name: Biking the Atlas Mountains and the Chegaga Dunes
  • Duration: 8 days, 6 days of cycling
  • Grade: Moderate
  • Best time to visit: March to December
  • Bike: Mountain bike, gravel bike or e-bike
  • Group size: 2 to 16 riders
  • Recommended age: 16 to 65
  • Start / finish: Marrakech
  • Accommodation: Hotels, a desert camp and a guesthouse (gîte)

itinerary_title.6: Erg Lihoudi to the Chegaga dunes and Foum Zguid
itinerary_title.7: Foum Zguid to Taznakht and Marrakech

itinerary_content.1:
We meet you at Marrakech Menara Airport and drive you to your hotel, 15 minutes away. In the evening your guide runs through the tour with the group. If you have time, wander through the old town, Bahia Palace and Jemaa el-Fna square.

Accommodation: Hotel or riad
Level: Easy
Drive: 15 minutes
Meals: Dinner
itinerary_content.2:
We leave the city and climb into the Atlas over the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260 m). The land turns dry and red as we reach Ait Ben Haddou, the old ksar you may know from Lawrence of Arabia and Gladiator. After lunch we get on the bikes and ride through small villages to Ouarzazate, the 'city of cinema'.

Accommodation: Kasbah hotel
Level: Moderate
Drive: 3.5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 45 km
itinerary_content.3:
A one-hour drive takes us to Tizi n'Tinifift (1,800 m), with a view over the volcanic Jebel Saghro and the Draa Valley, Morocco's longest valley at about 1,200 km. From there it's mostly downhill to the Tizgui waterfall and the first oasis. We ride through Berber villages and stop for mint tea with a local family.

Accommodation: Kasbah hotel
Level: Moderate
Drive: 1 hour
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 50 km
itinerary_content.4:
Today we follow the Draa oasis, where desert sand meets tall green palms. The river road gives some of the best views in southern Morocco. After 55 km on the bike, the 4x4 takes us the last 50 km to Zagora, the traditional gateway to the Sahara.

Accommodation: Kasbah hotel
Level: Moderate
Drive: 1 hour
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 55 km
itinerary_content.5:
Desert day. A short 4x4 drive takes us to Tamegroute and its Koranic library, which dates back to the 11th century. From there we ride into the Sahara on a varied route over dry lakes and past small green oases, all the way to our camp in the dunes of Erg Lihoudi. Dinner and the night are under the stars.

Accommodation: Camp
Level: Moderate
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 55 km
itinerary_content.6:
We drive 50 km across the dunes to Lake Iriqi, a dry salt lake where nomads still pass with their camels. Then we ride along the flat lakebed toward Foum Zguid, where we sleep in a kasbah hotel.

Accommodation: Kasbah hotel
Level: Moderate
Drive: 1.5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 65 km
itinerary_content.7:
The last ride is an easy 30 km through quiet oases and Berber villages. From Taznakht we drive back to Marrakech for the night.

Accommodation: Hotel or riad
Level: Moderate
Drive: 6 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch
Cycling distance: 30 km
itinerary_content.8:
Transfer to Menara Airport for your flight. Check-out is at 11:30. We hope to ride with you again – ma'a salama!

Drive: 15 minutes
Meals: Breakfast

tab_content.1_wpeditor:
This 8-day gravel bike tour starts and ends in Marrakech. You ride along the Atlas range and over the volcanic Jebel Saghro, following the old caravan road through quiet gorges, kasbahs and valleys until you reach the Draa Valley, Morocco's longest oasis.

It's a proper back-country route: five days of riding on dirt roads, with nights in kasbah hotels and family-run guesthouses.

itinerary_title.5: Jebel Saghro to the Draa Valley

itinerary_content.1:
We pick you up at Marrakech Menara Airport and drive you to the hotel. Later you meet your guide for a short briefing. With any time left, walk around the old town, Bahia Palace and Jemaa el-Fna square.

Accommodation: Hotel
Level: Easy
Drive: 20 minutes
itinerary_content.2:
We drive south over the High Atlas to the village of Ghassat, where the riding begins. The track runs over red earth and along the river to the Skoura oasis. It's an easy first day to find your rhythm. Night in a kasbah hotel.

Accommodation: Kasbah hotel
Level: Moderate
Drive: 5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 35 km
Elevation: +480 m / -490 m
itinerary_content.3:
A short drive takes us to Souk El Had. From there we ride across the Azaghar plateau, nomad country where some Berber families still live in caves. After lunch we continue through the Kati gorges and the Rose Valley to the Dades Gorges. Night in a guesthouse.

Accommodation: Guesthouse
Level: Moderate
Drive: 45 minutes
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 68 km
Elevation: +800 m / -490 m
itinerary_content.4:
We ride from the guesthouse toward the remote Berber villages of Jebel Saghro. A short climb to Boumalne Dades is followed by 15 flat kilometres. After tea with a local family, we cross the rocky Saghro massif to our guesthouse.

Accommodation: Guesthouse
Level: Moderate
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 68 km
Elevation: +1200 m / -1000 m
itinerary_content.5:
The day starts with a 5 km climb to the high Saghro plateau and wide views back to the High Atlas. After 15 km of rolling terrain, we drop down the old caravan route into the Draa Valley. Night in a kasbah hotel.

Accommodation: Kasbah hotel
Level: Moderate
Drive: 30 minutes
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 64 km
Elevation: +850 m / -650 m
itinerary_content.6:
An easy day, mostly flat or downhill, through the oasis and past old mud-brick villages. We stop for a picnic in the palm groves before reaching the Tizgui waterfall, then transfer to Ouarzazate for the night.

Accommodation: Hotel
Level: Moderate
Drive: 1 hour
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 46 km
Elevation: +400 m / -290 m
itinerary_content.7:
After breakfast we follow the caravan road through a green oasis to Ait Ben Haddou, famous as a film location. After lunch there's time for a walk through the old kasbah village, then we drive back to Marrakech.

Accommodation: Hotel
Level: Easy
Drive: 5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch
Walking: 1 hour
itinerary_content.8:
Transfer to Menara Airport for your flight. Check-out is at 11:30. We hope to see you on another gravel ride soon – ma'a salama!

Drive: 20 minutes
Meals: Breakfast

3761.title: Morocco Hike and Bike Tour: Happy Valley, Lake and Waterfall

tab_content.1_wpeditor:
Can't choose between hiking and cycling? This 8-day tour gives you both. You spend two full days walking in the Ait Bouguemez, the 'Happy Valley', below M'Goun (4,071 m), the second-highest mountain in Morocco. Then you ride for three days through the M'Goun Geopark to Bin El Ouidane lake and the Ouzoud waterfalls.

The walking is easy, the riding is moderate, and the 4x4 is always close by. It's a good choice for couples and groups with mixed fitness.

itinerary_content.1:
We meet you at Marrakech Menara Airport and drive you to your hotel, 15 minutes away. Later you meet your guide for a briefing about the tour. If you have time, visit the old town, Bahia Palace and Jemaa el-Fna square.

Level: Easy

itinerary_content.2:
A five-hour drive takes us into the mountains, with a stop at the natural bridge of Imi n'Ifri and lunch in the village of Ait Bouali. In the Happy Valley we meet the muleteers and walk for an hour to our guesthouse.

Accommodation: Guesthouse

Drive: 5 hours
Walking: 1 hour

itinerary_content.3:
A 4–5 hour walk takes us through the heart of the valley. We climb up to Sidi Moussa, an old hilltop granary where families kept their grain in small rooms. In the afternoon we walk up the valley from village to village to our guesthouse in Ait Imi.

Accommodation: Guesthouse
Level: Easy
Walking: 5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
itinerary_content.4:
We walk through the village of Ibaqalliwn to see dinosaur footprints left in the rock millions of years ago. Then we continue to Adazen for a great view of the valley. After lunch we go down to Zaouit Oulmzi for the night.

Accommodation: Guesthouse
Level: Easy
Walking: 5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
itinerary_content.5:
Breakfast on the terrace comes with a view of M'Goun (4,071 m). Then we get on the bikes. The first 8 km are easy, through potato fields and apple orchards. Then comes the hardest climb of the day, up to the Tizi n'Tirghist pass, with a big view of the Atlas range. After lunch a more technical stretch takes us up and down to our camp at Assamar.

Accommodation: Camp or hotel
Level: Moderate
Drive: 30 minutes
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 60 km
Elevation: +650 m / -650 m
itinerary_content.6:
Today's ride winds up and down through a long, quiet thuya forest on good gravel. It's a demanding but very rewarding day. We finish at the lake with a glass of mint tea at our hotel.

Accommodation: Hotel
Level: Moderate
Drive: 20 minutes
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Cycling distance: 50 km
Elevation: +550 m / -650 m
itinerary_content.7:
After a short transfer to Azilal, the last ride is mostly downhill through oak forests and olive groves, with a few short climbs. We reach the Ouzoud waterfalls in the early afternoon and have lunch with a view of the falls. Then we drive back to Marrakech, where the medina is at its liveliest in the evening.

Accommodation: Hotel
Level: Moderate
Drive: 2.5 hours
Walking: 1 hour
Meals: Breakfast, lunch
Cycling distance: 50 km
Elevation: +450 m / -780 m
itinerary_content.8:
Transfer to Menara Airport for your flight. Check-out is at 11:30. We hope to see you again soon – ma'a salama!

3727.title: Hike and Bike Morocco: Climb Toubkal and Ride the Agafay Desert

tab_content.1_wpeditor:
This tour starts and ends in Marrakech and packs a lot into eight days. First you trek for three days through the Azaden and Imnan valleys to the top of Toubkal (4,167 m), the highest peak in North Africa. Then you swap boots for a bike and ride two days through the Ouirgane valley and out into the stony Agafay desert.

The trek is challenging and the cycling is moderate. Mules carry the bags in the mountains, and a 4x4 supports you on the bike days.

itinerary_content.1:

itinerary_content.2:
After breakfast we drive about two hours to Imlil, where the trek starts. We meet the muleteers and walk for five hours over the Tizi Mzik pass (2,489 m / 8,166 ft), then down to our camp in the Tamsoult valley.

Accommodation: Camp
Level: Moderate
Drive: 2 hours
Walking: 5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +790 m / -300 m
itinerary_content.3:
A steady climb on an old mule path brings us to the Aguelzim pass (3,550 m), with a superb view of the Toubkal massif. After a picnic we go down to the refuge (3,207 m) and camp for the night.

Accommodation: Wild camp
Level: Moderate
Walking: 6.5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +1100 m / -300 m
itinerary_content.4:
Summit day. We start early and reach the top of Toubkal in about three and a half hours. On a clear day you can see for miles in every direction. After some time on the summit we go back down to the refuge for lunch, then continue to Aremd for a night in a guesthouse.

Accommodation: Guesthouse, Dar Aremd or similar
Level: Moderate to hard
Walking: 9 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +960 m / -2267 m
itinerary_content.5:
Now the bikes come out. We roll down to Imlil, then climb to the Tizi n'Tamatert pass (2,380 m) through the Berber villages of Ikiss and Tinghrin. Lunch is in the Imnan valley, with its terraced fields. After lunch a long, fun descent takes us to Asni, and a short transfer brings us to our guesthouse in the Ouirgane valley.
Note: If you want more riding, you can cycle the extra 18 km to the guesthouse.

Accommodation: Guesthouse or auberge
Level: Moderate
Cycling distance: 50 km
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +800 m / -1400 m
itinerary_content.6:
A short climb to the Tizi Ouadou pass (1,276 m) warms the legs, and we enjoy the view with a glass of mint tea. Then we ride down the valley to the Lalla Takerkoust lake for lunch by the water. In the afternoon we ride the last section into the Agafay desert and spend the night in a comfortable desert camp.

Accommodation: Luxury camp
Level: Moderate
Cycling distance: 45 km
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +750 m / -680 m
itinerary_content.7:
After breakfast we drive back to Marrakech for a city tour with a local guide: Bahia Palace, the Koutoubia mosque and the lanes of the old medina, ending at Jemaa el-Fna square.

Accommodation: Hotel
Level: Easy

3656.title: Hiking in the Ait Bouguemez Valley: Land of the Berbers

tab_content.1_wpeditor:
The Ait Bouguemez, better known as the Happy Valley, is a green valley about 30 km long in the central High Atlas, around 210 km east of Marrakech. Berber villages sit between the fields, and above them rises M'Goun, at over 4,070 m the second-highest mountain in Morocco.

This is a gentle trek. You walk four to five hours a day from village to village and sleep in family-run guesthouses, while mules carry the bags. You also visit the Ouzoud waterfalls and the natural bridge of Imi n'Ifri on the way.

3627.title: Toubkal Trek and Essaouira: 7 Days from Marrakech

tab_content.1_wpeditor:
Mountains first, then the sea. On this 7-day trip you trek for three days to the summit of Toubkal (4,167 m), the highest peak in North Africa. Then you spend two relaxed days in Essaouira, a laid-back fishing town on the Atlantic with a UNESCO-listed medina. The trip ends with a guided day in Marrakech.

It's a good way to earn your beach time. The climb is hard work, and the ocean breeze in Essaouira feels well deserved afterwards.

Elevation: +1457 m
itinerary_content.3:
Summit day. We leave around 2:30 am to reach the top for the best light. It takes about three and a half hours from camp to the summit (4,167 m). After enjoying the view we go back down to camp for lunch, then continue to the village of Aremd for the night.

Accommodation: Guesthouse
Level: Moderate to hard
Walking: 9.5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +960 m / -2267 m
itinerary_content.4:
A short walk takes us back to Imlil, then we travel to Essaouira on the Atlantic coast. The town used to be called Mogador. Its walled 18th-century medina is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and has long attracted artists.

Accommodation: Hotel
Level: Easy
Walking: 45 minutes
Drive: 3 hours
Meals: Breakfast
Elevation: -150 m
itinerary_content.5:
A free day to enjoy Essaouira, with a guided walk included. Photograph the sea walls, a mix of Portuguese and Berber design, and browse the souks, woodworking shops and art galleries. At the harbour, stalls grill the fish that just came in. In the afternoon, walk on the beach or just relax.

Accommodation: Hotel
Level: Easy
Walking: 4 hours
Meals: Breakfast
itinerary_content.6:
We drive back to Marrakech for a guided city tour. You'll see Jemaa el-Fna square, the 12th-century Koutoubia mosque and the 19th-century Bahia Palace, have a traditional lunch and walk through the souks. The rest of the afternoon is free.

Accommodation: Hotel
Level: Easy
Walking: 3 hours
Drive: 3 hours
Meals: Breakfast
itinerary_content.7:
Transfer to the airport for your flight home.

Meals: Breakfast

3621.title: Sahara Desert Trek: Walking with Camels from M'Hamid

tab_content.1_wpeditor:
Four days walking in the Sahara with a camel caravan, far from roads and towns. From M'Hamid El Ghizlane we follow dry riverbeds and cross big dunes. At night we sleep in nomad tents under more stars than you have ever seen.

The walking is easy, about five hours a day, and the camels carry the bags. You can also ride a camel for a while if your feet need a rest. On the way there and back you cross the High Atlas and visit the Draa oasis and Ait Ben Haddou.

Trip details

  • Tour name: Moroccan Sahara Desert Trek
  • Duration: 8 days
  • Grade: Easy
  • Best time to visit: September to May
  • Type of travel: Trekking
  • Group size: Usually 2 to 16 people
  • Recommended age: 8 to 75
  • Start / finish: Marrakech
  • Accommodation: Hotel or riad, and desert camps during the trek

cost.cost_includes:
Meals: 7 breakfasts, 7 lunches and 6 dinners, plus water during the trek
Accommodation: 3 nights in hotels and 4 nights in camps
Transport by comfortable van or Toyota 4x4
A visit to the old medina of Marrakech, 4 days of trekking in the Sahara, a tour of Ait Ben Haddou and a camel ride in the desert
cost.cost_excludes:
Flights

Personal travel insurance

trip_highlights.highlight_text: Explore the medina of Marrakech
Cross the High Atlas Mountains
Visit the film studios of Ouarzazate
See Ait Ben Haddou, a famous film location
Trek through the Sahara with camels
Visit the Draa oasis

itinerary_title.2: Marrakech to M'Hamid and the Draa oasis
itinerary_title.6: Erg Smar to Oulad Driss, transfer to Agdz
itinerary_title.7: Agdz to Marrakech via Ait Ben Haddou

itinerary_content.1:
Welcome to Marrakech, the Red City. Look for the We Gravel Morocco sign at Menara Airport, and we'll drive you to your hotel. Explore the city if you like before the welcome meeting, where you meet your guide and go through the trip.

Accommodation: Hotel
Level: Easy
Drive: 20 minutes
itinerary_content.2:
A long but beautiful drive today. We cross the High Atlas over the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260 m), the highest road pass in Morocco. We stop for lunch in the big palm groves of the Draa Valley, then continue to Ras Nkhal on the edge of the Sahara. First night in camp.

Accommodation: Camp
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Level: Easy
Drive: 9 hours
Walking: 45 minutes
itinerary_content.3:
The trek begins. Once the camels are loaded, we walk through golden dunes to the big dune of Erg Mado and climb it for a wide view over the desert. Lunch is a picnic in the shade of tamarisk trees. Night in camp.

Accommodation: Camp
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Level: Easy
Walking: 5 hours
itinerary_content.4:
We follow the camels across stony plateaus and climb the dune of Erg Zahar for another great view. Night in camp.

Accommodation: Camp
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Level: Easy
Walking: 5 hours
itinerary_content.5:
Get up early for the sunrise and have breakfast in the open air. Then we walk deeper into the desert along the dry bed of the Draa River. You can ride a camel for a while, and the camel men will show you how they bake bread in the hot sand. Night in camp.

Accommodation: Camp
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Level: Easy
Walking: 5 hours
itinerary_content.6:
After breakfast we walk for an hour and a half to Oulad Driss and say goodbye to the caravan team. Then we drive to the Agdz oasis and spend the night in a kasbah.

Accommodation: Kasbah
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Level: Easy
Drive: 5 hours
itinerary_content.7:
We follow the old caravan road through a green oasis to Ait Ben Haddou, the ksar used in many films. After lunch we walk through the old village, then drive on to Marrakech.

Accommodation: Hotel
Meals: Breakfast
Level: Easy
Drive: 6 hours
Walking: 1 hour
itinerary_content.8:
Transfer to the airport for your flight home.

Meals: Breakfast
Drive: 20 minutes

3616.title: Climb Mount Toubkal: 6-Day Trek from Marrakech

tab_content.1_wpeditor:
Toubkal (4,167 m) is the highest mountain in Morocco and in North Africa. This 6-day trip takes the quieter route to the top, over the Tizi Mzik and Aguelzim passes, through Toubkal National Park and past Berber villages and high valleys.

Before and after the trek you have time in Marrakech, with a guided tour of its palaces, gardens, souks and Jemaa el-Fna square. The trip ends with a farewell dinner.

Trip details

  • Tour name: Climb Mount Toubkal
  • Duration: 6 days, 5 nights, 3 days of trekking
  • Grade: Moderate to hard
  • Best time to visit: March to November
  • Type of travel: Trekking
  • Group size: 2 to 16 people
  • Recommended age: 18 to 75
  • Start / finish: Marrakech
  • Accommodation: Guesthouse, camp and riad

cost.cost_includes:
Meals: 5 breakfasts, 4 lunches and 5 dinners, plus mineral water during the trek
Accommodation: 2 nights in a riad, 1 night in a guesthouse and 2 nights in camps
Transport: airport transfer, Marrakech to Imlil and back by comfortable van or 4x4, plus mules and muleteers during the trek
The guided climb of Toubkal and a guided tour of Marrakech

trip_highlights.highlight_text: Explore the lanes of the old medina of Marrakech
See how Berber families live in the mountains
Climb the highest mountain in North Africa
Farewell dinner with live music and oriental dance

itinerary_title.2: Marrakech (450 m) to Azib Tamsoult (2,400 m)
itinerary_title.3: Azib Tamsoult to the Aguelzim pass (3,550 m) and the Toubkal refuge (3,207 m)
itinerary_title.4: Toubkal summit (4,167 m) and Aremd (1,900 m)

itinerary_content.1:
Welcome to Marrakech, the Red City. Look for the We Gravel Morocco sign at Menara Airport, and we'll drive you to your riad. Explore the city if you like, then meet the group and your guide to go through the trip.

Accommodation: Riad or hotel
Level: Easy
Meals: Dinner
itinerary_content.2:
After breakfast we drive to Imlil and meet the muleteers. We walk up to the Tizi Mzik pass (2,450 m) and have lunch with a view over the Imnan valley. Then we continue to Azib Tamsoult and camp for the night.

Accommodation: Camp
Level: Easy to moderate
Drive: 1.5 hours
Walking: 6 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +750 m / -350 m
itinerary_content.3:
A steady climb on an old mule path brings us to the Aguelzim pass, with a superb view of the Toubkal massif. After a picnic we go down to the refuge and camp for the night.

Accommodation: Wild camp
Level: Moderate
Walking: 6.5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +1100 m / -300 m
itinerary_content.4:
Summit day. We start early and reach the top in about three and a half hours. On a clear day you can see for miles in every direction. After some time on the summit we go back down to the refuge for lunch, then continue to Aremd for a night in a guesthouse.

Accommodation: Guesthouse, Dar Aremd or similar
Level: Moderate to hard
Walking: 9 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +960 m / -2267 m
itinerary_content.5:
A short walk down the valley brings us back to Imlil, where the trek ends. We drive to Marrakech, and after lunch you have a guided tour of the city's mosques, palaces and gardens. Then you're free to explore until the farewell dinner.

Accommodation: Riad or hotel
Level: Easy
Drive: 1.5 hours
Walking: 45 minutes
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
itinerary_content.6:
Transfer to the airport, depending on your flight time.

Meals: Breakfast

3611.title: Classic Toubkal Trek: 3 Days from Marrakech

tab_content.1_wpeditor:
This is the classic Toubkal trek, and the quickest way to stand on the roof of North Africa. In three days you walk from Imlil up through Berber villages and a rocky high valley to the summit of Toubkal (4,167 m), then back down again.

It's hard work but not technical. Mules carry the bags, and you sleep one night at the base camp and one in a village guesthouse. If you're short on time but want a real mountain, this is the trip for you.

Trip details

  • Tour name: Classic Toubkal Climb
  • Duration: 3 days, 2 nights
  • Grade: Moderate to hard
  • Best time to visit: March to November
  • Type of travel: Trekking
  • Group size: 2 to 16 people
  • Recommended age: 16 to 70
  • Start / finish: Marrakech or Imlil
  • Accommodation: Guesthouse and camp

Meals: 2 breakfasts, 2 lunches and 2 dinners, plus mineral water during the trek
Accommodation: 1 night in a guesthouse and 1 night in a camp
Transport by comfortable van or 4x4, plus mules and muleteers during the trek
The guided climb of Toubkal

trip_highlights.highlight_text: Climb Toubkal (4,167 m), the highest peak in North Africa
Walk through traditional Berber villages
Explore Marrakech before or after the trek

itinerary_title.1: Marrakech to Imlil (1,750 m) and the Toubkal base camp (3,207 m)
itinerary_title.2: Toubkal summit (4,167 m) and Aremd (1,900 m)

itinerary_content.1:
We pick you up from your hotel or riad in Marrakech and drive about an hour and a half to Imlil. There you meet the muleteers and start a five-hour walk to the base camp. We pass the village of Aremd (1,950 m) and stop for lunch at the shrine of Sidi Chamharouch (2,360 m), then zigzag up to the base camp. You sleep in the refuge, or in a tent if you prefer, from May to the end of October.

Accommodation: Camping
Level: Moderate to hard
Drive: 1.5 hours
Walking: 5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +1457 m
itinerary_content.2:
We start early for the summit of Toubkal, the highest point in the Atlas and in North Africa. From the top, the views stretch across the Atlas toward the Sahara. We go back down to the refuge for lunch, then continue to Aremd for the night.

Accommodation: Guesthouse
Level: Moderate to hard
Walking: 9 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +960 m / -2217 m
itinerary_content.3:
After breakfast at the guesthouse we walk down to Imlil and drive about an hour and a half back to Marrakech, arriving around midday. Add a guided tour of the medina if you'd like to see more of the city.

Level: Easy
Drive: 1.5 hours
Walking: 45 minutes
Meals: Breakfast
Elevation: -150 m

tab_content.1_wpeditor:
M'Goun (4,071 m) is the second-highest mountain in North Africa, and much quieter than Toubkal. On this 8-day trek you walk up from the green Ait Bouguemez valley, cross passes above 3,400 m, follow old nomad paths and camp on high plateaus before the summit day.

The route is wild and varied. You see green fields, Berber villages, deep valleys and open high mountains. On the way in and out you also visit the natural bridge of Imi n'Ifri and the Ouzoud waterfalls.

Trip details

  • Tour name: Mount M'Goun Trek
  • Duration: 8 days, 7 nights, 5 days of trekking
  • Grade: Moderate to hard
  • Best time to visit: June to October
  • Type of travel: Trekking
  • Group size: 2 to 16 people
  • Recommended age: 18 to 80
  • Start / finish: Marrakech
  • Accommodation: Guesthouse, camps and a hotel or riad

Accommodation: 2 nights in a hotel, 1 night in a guesthouse and 4 nights in camps

The guided climb of M'Goun

trip_highlights.highlight_text: Visit the imperial city of Marrakech
Hike through remote high-mountain landscapes
Climb the second-highest peak in North Africa
Walk on old nomad paths
See the natural bridge of Imi n'Ifri
Visit the Ouzoud waterfalls

itinerary_title.2: Marrakech to the Ait Bouguemez valley via Imi n'Ifri
itinerary_title.3: Ikiss (2,250 m) to the Tarkdit plateau (2,900 m)
itinerary_title.4: M'Goun summit (4,071 m) to Oulilimt (2,600 m)
itinerary_title.5: Oulilimt (2,600 m) to Ain Aflafal (2,300 m)
itinerary_title.6: Ain Aflafal (2,300 m) to Tabant (2,000 m)
itinerary_title.7: Tabant to Marrakech via Azilal and the Ouzoud waterfalls

itinerary_content.1:
Your driver meets you at Menara Airport and takes you to your hotel. In the late afternoon your mountain guide briefs you on the trek, and in the evening you sit down to your first Moroccan dinner.

Accommodation: Hotel or riad
Level: Easy
Meals: Dinner
itinerary_content.2:
We leave the city behind and drive to the foothills of the central High Atlas. On the way we stop at Imi n'Ifri, a natural limestone bridge carved by the river that still flows under it. We have a picnic after a short walk across the bridge, then drive up into the hidden Ait Bouguemez valley. After mint tea with the muleteers, we walk up the Arous gorge to the pastures of Azib n'Ikiss (2,250 m) and camp for the night.

Accommodation: Camp
Level: Easy
Walking: 2.5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +450 m
itinerary_content.3:
The bags go on the mules and we climb steadily for about three hours to the Aghouri pass (3,400 m), with our first view of the M'Goun summit. After a slow picnic we follow a nomad path down to the Tarkdit plateau and camp.

Accommodation: Camp
Level: Moderate
Walking: 5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +1150 m / -500 m
itinerary_content.4:
The big day. The climb isn't technical but the trail is steep, and it's a long, tough mountain day. From the top the view takes in the High Atlas, the Anti-Atlas and the Rose Valley. We go down to the Oulilimt valley to camp.
Note: If you'd rather skip the summit, you can walk with the muleteers to the next camp, an easier walk of about 5–6 hours.

Accommodation: Camp
Level: Moderate to hard
Walking: 9 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +1171 m / -1471 m
itinerary_content.5:
We start by going down to Tighramt, below M'Goun, then walk an easy five hours through the wild Oulilimt valley to Ain Aflafal, with a picnic by the river on the way. Night in camp at Tighramt n'Ait Hemd.

Accommodation: Camp
Level: Easy
Walking: 5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +240 m / -300 m
itinerary_content.6:
We head back to the Happy Valley over the Tizi n'Ait Imi pass (2,900 m). The 550 m climb is rewarded with a great view over the M'Goun range. After a picnic at the pass, a 950 m descent brings us to Tabant, the main village of the valley and the end of the trek. Night in a guesthouse.

Accommodation: Guesthouse
Level: Moderate
Walking: 6.5 hours
Meals: Breakfast, lunch, dinner
Elevation: +600 m / -1050 m
itinerary_content.7:
We say goodbye to the trekking team and drive back to Marrakech via Azilal and the Ouzoud waterfalls. You reach your hotel in the early afternoon, with time to visit the medina and Jemaa el-Fna square before the farewell dinner.

Accommodation: Hotel or riad
Level: Easy
Meals: Breakfast, lunch
itinerary_content.8:
Transfer to the airport, depending on your flight time.

Meals: Breakfast
